newsitem.title: USA: Iowa racetrack worth $160 mln could be sold. [CORRECTED 22:31 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Iowa racetrack worth $160 mln could be sold. [CORRECTED 22:31 GMT]

text.p: A government-owned race track and casino in Altoona, Iowa, has been appraised at $160 million and Polk County supervisors are expected to decide in June whether to sell the highly profitable facility, county spokesman Phil Roeder said Wednesday.

The Prairie Meadows Race Track had been on the verge of bankruptcy until installation of slot machines in 1995 began a massive turnaround that has allowed the county to put aside enough money to retire all the debt issued for it.
Polk County had sold $26.5 million of gaming revenue bonds in 1995 and $38.8 million of tax-exempt general obligation bonds in 1993 for the facility.

"We expect sometime in June that the board is going to decide if we are going to retain it, and continue to own and manage the casino, or if we are going to put a 'for sale' sign in front," Roeder said.
The track's profitability attracted an offer from Circus Circus Enterprises Inc., a Las Vegas-based gaming company, in September 1996, which was later withdrawn.

Polk County supervisors sought an appraisal for the property and received a report Tuesday from Hospitality Real Estate Counselors of Thornton (corrects from "Morton"), Colo., and Urban Systems Inc. of New Orleans, Roeder said.
The land, buildings, equipment and gaming licenses were valued at $160 million, Roeder said.
The appraisers also projected revenues of $123.5 million for 1997, $127.25 million in 1998 and $143.2 million in 2002 if Prairie Meadows continues to have 1,100 slot machines, Roeder said.
If another 400 slot machines were added to the facility in 1998, as is under consideration, the projections rise to $142.3 million in 1998 and $159.99 million in 2002, Roeder said.
Roeder called the $160 million appraisal "narrow" and said supervisors would expect more before selling Prairie Meadows.
"I think the board is of strong opinion that certainly it is worth more than that to the community and I don't think anyone should anticipate an asking price of $160 million," Roeder said.
"It would be definitely above that for them to seriously consider an offer," Roeder said.
Later in May, supervisors expect to receive a report on the economic impact on Polk County if they sell Prairie Meadows to a private owner, Roeder said.
The upcoming report will look at the impact on property tax revenues, area businesses and entertainment facilities, Roeder said.
